title: Define cross-crate capability contract ownership
purpose: Turn the functional matrix into an ownership contract that prevents future features from re-coupling agentd and runtime logic.
scope: Define which data types belong in runtime_contracts.
Define which workflow state belongs in agent_core.
Define which execution authority belongs in security_execution.
Define which CLI/TUI/API surfaces belong in agentd.
Add a reviewer checklist for future capability PRs.
implementation_steps: Write a cross-crate ownership table with allowed and forbidden responsibilities.
Add examples for package, content, Firecracker, diagnostics, and operator workflows.
Add a PR checklist requiring typed contract, policy mapping, audit projection, and gate evidence.
Record evidence with the contract hash and open questions.
acceptance_criteria: The contract explains why agentd must not own adapter business logic.
The contract identifies the first files likely to change per capability family.
The PR checklist is concrete enough to block bypass paths.
The evidence lists any intentional exceptions.
verification: Run `cargo test --workspace` after future code work touches these boundaries.
Check the document references all four crates.
failure_modes: Contract repeats architecture slogans without file-level ownership.
Agentd is allowed to mutate host state directly.
runtime_contracts starts depending on execution crates.
SecurityExecution starts owning product workflow branching.
